en.字龕:
### 聖 *shèng* — the sage

**字 Graph** ｜ 篆 ![聖之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E8%81%96.svg)

**文 Gloss** ｜ The *Shuowen*: 「聖，通也。從耳，呈聲。」 — "To be through-open. From 耳, the ear; 呈 as sound."

**像 Image** ｜ The sage's graph is built on an ear — not an eye, not a mouth. 聖 is the one who hears through: everything, from everyone, without blockage.

**義 Sense** ｜ A sage "constantly without heart of his own, taking the hundred clans' heart as his heart" is exactly what the graph promises: rule by listening. He does not look down upon the people; he hears them in.

### 心 *xīn* — heart

**字 Graph** ｜ 篆 ![心之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E5%BF%83.svg)

**文 Gloss** ｜ The *Shuowen*: 「人心，土藏，在身之中。象形。博士說以爲火藏。」 — "The human heart: the earth-organ, in the middle of the body. A picture. The Academicians take it for the fire-organ."

**像 Image** ｜ The graph is the organ itself, and its gloss carries a debate — earth-organ, the still center that receives, or fire-organ, the flame that climbs and shines — as if the lexicon already knew the heart can be either: seat, or blaze.

**義 Sense** ｜ 无心 does not cut the heart out; it stills the blaze into the seat. The sage's heart is the earth-organ: a center, not a fire.

en.校記:
Manuscript A (MS A) is badly damaged in the first half of this chapter, which therefore largely follows Manuscript B (MS B); 善者善之 and everything from 聖人之在天下 on follow MS A, and lacunae common to both are kept. Graphs are those outside the brackets in the *Changsha Mawangdui Han mu jianbo jicheng* (2014; hereafter *Jicheng*).

- 𦔻人恆无心: Follows MS B. The line is wholly lost in MS A, where the original editors restored it from MS B. MS B's 𦔻, restored as 聖 in the 1980 edition, is read directly in the *Jicheng* from the mirror-image offset on the backing silk and taken as 聖 "sage". Wang Bi reads 聖人無常心 "the sage has no constant heart". (*Jicheng* IV, p. 18, n. 56; p. 200, n. 44)
- 以百眚之心為心: Follows MS B; 眚 is read as 姓, "the hundred clans". In MS A the trace above 以 cannot belong to 心 and may be the remains of 乃, so the *Jicheng* inserts a lacuna between the restored 心 of the previous line and 以; MS A's 姓 is read directly from a newly joined fragment. Wang Bi reads 以百姓心為心. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 18, n. 57)
- 善者善之: Follows MS A; MS B keeps only 善. Wang Bi reads 善者，吾善之; neither silk manuscript has 吾 "I" in this line or the three that follow.
- 不善者亦善□: Follows MS A, whose last graph is lost; the whole line is lost in MS B.
- 德善也: Follows MS B. The 1980 edition restored the graph before 善也 in MS B as 得 after the Fu Yi and other texts; a fragment stuck to the backing silk, bearing most of 德 and the right side of 善, belongs here, and the *Jicheng* reads 德. In MS A the graph is lost; it was probably 德, though 得 cannot be ruled out, and the *Jicheng* gives □. Wang Bi reads 德善. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 18, n. 58; p. 200, n. 45)
- 信者信之 / 不信者亦信之: Follows MS B. MS A keeps 亦信, formerly bracketed as a restoration and now read directly from a newly joined small fragment. Wang Bi reads 信者，吾信之；不信者，吾亦信之. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 18, n. 58)
- 德信也: Follows MS B. The 1980 edition glossed 德 as 得; the *Jicheng*, as a precaution, gives no gloss. MS A keeps 信也, with the graph above it given as □. Wang Bi reads 德信. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 18, n. 58; p. 200, n. 46)
- 聖人之在天下翕翕焉: Follows MS A; the *Jicheng* reads 聖人 directly. MS A writes 翕 with a repetition mark, here written out; on the colour plate the graph has 合 above 羽, with no heart radical, so the earlier transcription 愉 was wrong. MS B reads 𦔻人之在天下也欲﹦焉, with 也 and with 欲欲 for 翕翕. Wang Bi reads 聖人在天下歙歙.
- 為天下渾心: Follows MS A; lost in MS B. Wang Bi reads 為天下渾其心.
- 百姓皆屬耳目焉: Follows MS A. MS B reads □生皆注亓□□□, with 生 for 姓 and 注 "poured toward" for 屬 "fastened". Wang Bi reads 百姓皆注其耳目.
- 聖人皆□之: Damaged in both. In MS A the *Jicheng* reads 皆 and 之 directly; of the graph between them only a very little ink at the left survives, which is not the 口 component and cannot be confirmed as 亥. The original editors read 咳 after the Fu Yi text; the *Jicheng* gives □, and the colour plate does not bear out 咳. For MS B the 1980 edition restored 人皆咳之; the *Jicheng* reads 人, 皆 and 之 directly from the offset, the graph between being unclear there, and gives □. Wang Bi reads 聖人皆孩之. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 19, n. 60; p. 200, n. 47)
en.疏:
杳眇曰：

「𦔻人恆无心，以百眚之心為心」（乙本；𦔻讀為聖，眚讀為姓）——此一章之綱領，亦老子政治哲學之極則。

夫「恆无心」者，非痴愚之無心，乃虛己以應物之無心也。虛己故無私意，無私意故無偏情，無偏情故天下之心自赴之，此聖人所以為聖也。聖人之心，虛無恬淡，無有固必。然帛書作「恆无心」，王弼作「無常心」——語序既殊，義亦有別。恆无心者，心體恆虛，無時而非無；無常心者，心無定守，猶可移易。前者究竟，後者稍遜，帛書義深於王弼明矣。此與《大學》「所藏乎身不恕」相發明——恕者推己以及人，聖人則並己而化之，直以百姓之心為心，未嘗有能所之分也。

善者善之，不善者亦善之，此德善也。信者信之，不信者亦信之，此德信也。善與不善，待之如一；信與不信，報之以誠。非濫用寬容，乃道之自現：聖人不執善惡之名，唯視其能歸。歸者即善，未歸者非不屑，待之如赤子而引之，使自返於道，此善之至也。水善利萬物而有靜，聖人善化百姓而不棄，其揆一也。

「聖人在天下，歙歙焉為天下渾心」——歙歙者，收斂氣息之貌；渾心者，使天下之心渾然歸一也。百姓萬殊，聖人抱一以御之；耳目日馳，聖人渾之使返。帛書甲本云「百姓皆屬耳目焉」，乙本與王弼作「注」。屬者，繫屬也，言百姓之心為耳目之欲所拘；注者，灌注也，義稍淺。帛書「屬」字義長。

「聖人皆咳之」——帛書甲本此句作「聖人皆□之」，「皆」「之」二字據殘筆釋出，中一字唯餘殘筆，1980 年整理者擬讀為「咳」，《集成》改作闕文；乙本亦作「□人皆□之」；王弼作「孩」。若從舊讀，咳者，小兒笑之聲，動而未成之言；孩者，赤子之狀，靜而無知之時。聖人視天下之民，皆如其初生之初，無有賢不肖之分，不責其陷溺，而欣然引之使出。嗚呼！世人患有好惡，聖人廓然大公；世人患有分別，聖人與不善不信皆善皆信。不爭之德，於斯為盛，百姓自歸，如嬰兒之就其母，夫何為哉。
en.疏英:
Yaomiao says:

"The sage is constantly without heart of his own; he takes the hundred clans' heart as his heart": the headline of the chapter, and the utmost rule of Laozi's politics.

"Constantly without heart" is no idiot blankness; it is the no-heart that empties the self to answer things. Empty of self, hence without private intent; without private intent, hence without partial feeling; without partial feeling — and the hearts of all-under-heaven come to him of themselves. This is what makes the sage a sage. The sage's heart is empty and calm, holding nothing fixed or necessary. But the silk text writes 恆无心, "constantly without heart," where Wang Bi has 無常心, "without a constant heart": the word order differs, and so does the sense. Constantly-without-heart: the heart's substance is forever empty, no moment not 无. Without-a-constant-heart: a heart with no fixed holding, which might yet shift. The first is final; the second falls short; the silk text plainly runs deeper. Read it against the Great Learning's "what is stored in the self, not extended to others": 恕 extends from self to others, but the sage dissolves even the self, and takes the hundred clans' heart directly as his own, with no remainder of doer and done-to.

To the good he is good, to the not-good he is also good: this is the good of De. The trustworthy he trusts, the untrustworthy he also trusts: this is the trust of De. Good and not-good are met as one; trust and no-trust are answered with sincerity. This is no promiscuous tolerance: it is the Dao showing itself. The sage does not grip the names "good" and "evil"; he watches only whether a man can come home. The one who returns is good; the one not yet returned is not despised — he is met like a naked babe and led, until he turns back to the Dao of himself. That is goodness at its utmost. Water benefits the ten thousand things and keeps still; the sage transforms the hundred clans and discards none: one gauge.

"The sage, in all-under-heaven, draws his breath in and in, and for all-under-heaven muddles his heart into one": 歙歙 is the look of breath gathered inward; 渾心 is making the hearts of all-under-heaven turn whole and one. The hundred clans are ten-thousandfold; the sage holds the One to steer them. Ears and eyes gallop daily; the sage muddles them back toward home. Silk manuscript A says 百姓皆屬耳目焉: 屬, "fastened": the clans' hearts tied up in the appetites of ear and eye. Manuscript B and Wang Bi write 注, "poured toward," a shallower sense. The silk text's graph carries more.

"The sage receives them all as 咳": manuscript A reads 聖人皆□之 — 皆 and 之 are read from their traces, but the graph between survives only as broken strokes; the 1980 editors restored it as 咳, and the 2014 *Jicheng* leaves it unread (manuscript B likewise has □人皆□之). If we follow the old reading, 咳 is the sound of an infant's laugh, motion before speech is formed; Wang Bi's 孩 is the babe's state, stillness before knowing. The sage looks on the people of all-under-heaven as each at the moment of its first birth — no division of worthy and unworthy, no blame for their sinking, only the glad hand drawing them out. Ah — the world's disease is having likes and hates; the sage is open and wholly impartial. The world's disease is drawing distinctions; the sage is good to the not-good and trusts the untrustworthy. The De of not contending is at its fullest here; the hundred clans come home of themselves, as an infant to its mother — and what has he *done*?
en.英譯:
The sage is constantly without heart of his own: he takes the hundred clans' heart as his heart.

To the good he is good; to the not-good he is also good: this is the good of De. The trustworthy he trusts; the untrustworthy he also trusts: this is the trust of De.

The sage, in all-under-heaven, draws his breath in and in (翕翕), and for all-under-heaven muddles his heart into one. The hundred clans are all bound to their ears and eyes; the sage meets them all as infants at their first laugh (咳 — the 1980 editors' restoration; the silk is torn here, and the 2014 *Jicheng* leaves the graph unread).

校記:
本章帛書原文前半甲本殘甚而多據乙本，「善者善之」及「聖人之在天下」以下據甲本，二本皆殘者存其闕；字從《集成》（2014）括號外原字。

- 𦔻人恆无心：從乙本。甲本此句全殘，原整理者據乙本補之。乙本「𦔻」字原作補文「聖」，《集成》據襯頁反印文直接釋出，讀為「聖」。王弼本作「聖人無常心」。（《集成》肆·頁18·注56；頁200·注44）
- 以百眚之心為心：從乙本，「眚」讀為「姓」。甲本「以」上殘筆決不屬「心」字，或是「乃」字之殘，《集成》於上句末「心」與「以」間加一□；甲本「姓」字據新綴碎片直接釋出。王弼本作「以百姓心為心」。（《集成》肆·頁18·注57）
- 善者善之：從甲本；乙本唯存「善」字。王弼本作「善者，吾善之」，帛書此句及下三句皆無「吾」字。
- 不善者亦善□：從甲本，末字殘；乙本全句殘。
- 德善也：從乙本。乙本「善也」上之字，原釋文據傅奕本等補作「得」；襯頁所粘殘片存「德」字大半與「善」字右部，綴入此處，《集成》改釋為「德」。甲本此字殘，大概是「德」，然不排除為「得」，《集成》作□。王弼本作「德善」。（《集成》肆·頁18·注58；頁200·注45）
- 信者信之　不信者亦信之：從乙本。甲本存「亦信」二字，原作補文，《集成》據新綴小殘片直接釋出。王弼本作「信者，吾信之；不信者，吾亦信之」。（《集成》肆·頁18·注58）
- 德信也：從乙本。原釋文於「德」下括注「得」，《集成》為謹慎計暫不括注。甲本存「信也」，其上之字作□。王弼本作「德信」。（《集成》肆·頁18·注58；頁200·注46）
- 聖人之在天下翕翕焉：從甲本，「聖人」二字《集成》直接釋出。甲本「翕」下有重文號，今展開；其字彩版上从合、下从羽，無忄旁，舊錄作「愉」，誤。乙本作「𦔻人之在天下也欲﹦焉」，有「也」字，「翕翕」作「欲欲」。王弼本作「聖人在天下歙歙」。
- 為天下渾心：從甲本；乙本殘。王弼本作「為天下渾其心」。
- 百姓皆屬耳目焉：從甲本。乙本作「□生皆注亓□□□」，「生」讀為「姓」，「屬」作「注」。王弼本作「百姓皆注其耳目」。
- 聖人皆□之：二本皆殘。甲本「皆」「之」二字直接釋出，中一字只剩左側極少殘墨，非「口」旁，亦不能定為「亥」旁；原整理者據傅奕本釋為「咳」，《集成》改作□，彩版亦不能證「咳」。乙本原釋文補作「人皆咳之」，《集成》據反印文直接釋出「人」「皆」「之」三字，中一字反印文不清，作□。王弼本作「聖人皆孩之」。（《集成》肆·頁19·注60；頁200·注47）

疏:
杳眇曰：

「𦔻人恆无心，以百眚之心為心」（乙本；𦔻讀為聖，眚讀為姓）——此一章之綱領，亦老子政治哲學之極則。

夫「恆无心」者，非痴愚之無心，乃虛己以應物之無心也。虛己故無私意，無私意故無偏情，無偏情故天下之心自赴之，此聖人所以為聖也。聖人之心，虛無恬淡，無有固必。然帛書作「恆无心」，王弼作「無常心」——語序既殊，義亦有別。恆无心者，心體恆虛，無時而非無；無常心者，心無定守，猶可移易。前者究竟，後者稍遜，帛書義深於王弼明矣。此與《[[大學]]》「所藏乎身不恕」相發明——恕者推己以及人，聖人則並己而化之，直以百姓之心為心，未嘗有能所之分也。

善者善之，不善者亦善之，此德善也。信者信之，不信者亦信之，此德信也。善與不善，待之如一；信與不信，報之以誠。非濫用寬容，乃道之自現：聖人不執善惡之名，唯視其能歸。歸者即善，未歸者非不屑，待之如赤子而引之，使自返於道，此善之至也。水善利萬物而有靜，聖人善化百姓而不棄，其揆一也。

「聖人在天下，歙歙焉為天下渾心」——歙歙者，收斂氣息之貌；渾心者，使天下之心渾然歸一也。百姓萬殊，聖人抱一以御之；耳目日馳，聖人渾之使返。帛書甲本云「百姓皆屬耳目焉」，乙本與王弼作「注」。屬者，繫屬也，言百姓之心為耳目之欲所拘；注者，灌注也，義稍淺。帛書「屬」字義長。

「聖人皆咳之」——帛書甲本此句作「聖人皆□之」，「皆」「之」二字據殘筆釋出，中一字唯餘殘筆，1980 年整理者擬讀為「咳」，《集成》改作闕文；乙本亦作「□人皆□之」；王弼作「孩」。若從舊讀，咳者，小兒笑之聲，動而未成之言；孩者，赤子之狀，靜而無知之時。聖人視天下之民，皆如其初生之初，無有賢不肖之分，不責其陷溺，而欣然引之使出。嗚呼！世人患有好惡，聖人廓然大公；世人患有分別，聖人與不善不信皆善皆信。[[不爭之德]]，於斯為盛，百姓自歸，如嬰兒之就其母，夫何為哉。
